title: Add GitHub artifact attestations when supported
description: Add provenance attestation for published release artifacts when the repository and GitHub settings support it, without treating attestation as a replacement for checksum or security review.
acceptanceCriteria: The release workflow requests the minimum required `id-token` and `attestations` permissions
Each published artifact is covered by a provenance attestation or the workflow records an explicit unsupported-skip reason
The installer/documentation explains how to verify checksum and, when available, `gh attestation verify`
A failed attestation step blocks publication

steps.details: Assert that a release with attestation support declares the required permissions and a post-build attestation step before release creation.
Add a safe conditional step using the repository's supported GitHub mechanism, pinning the action to an immutable commit SHA and binding the subject digest.
Document checksum verification first and optional provenance verification without claiming attestation proves code safety.
Run the workflow fixture and a local checksum verification; record any GitHub-only limitation as an evidence gap.

technicalNotes: Do not add a signing key or secret to the repository. If the repository setting does not support attestations, fail the release gate or record an explicit owner-approved waiver.
